definition: AI in legal technology — contract review, e-discovery, legal research, and compliance monitoring.
details: AI in legal technology — contract review, e-discovery, legal research, and compliance monitoring.

explainer.lead: AI legal technology uses software to help people review contracts, find evidence, research law, and watch for compliance issues. It can reduce repetitive reading and searching, while leaving important legal judgments and checks to people.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a very fast helper reading a huge pile of school rules and permission slips to find the parts you need. In legal work, AI can similarly search documents, highlight useful passages, and organize information. A person still needs to check its work before making an important decision.
tiers.practitioner: Applications typically take legal documents, search requests, or compliance records as input and produce candidate passages, document classifications, summaries, or alerts for review. These outputs should be treated as decision support: incomplete retrieval, misread clauses, and incorrect legal interpretations can pass downstream unless reviewers validate them. Access controls and careful handling matter because the inputs can contain sensitive legal material.
tiers.paperLevel: AI legal technology can be described as AI-assisted functions over legal inputs: f(x) -> y, where x contains documents, research queries, or compliance records and y contains retrieved passages, classifications, extracted clauses, summaries, or alerts. Its main task areas are contract review, e-discovery, legal research, and compliance monitoring. Outputs are assistive rather than inherently authoritative, and evaluation must account for both missed relevant material and incorrect or unsupported results.

explainer.example: A reviewer asks a contract-review system to find termination clauses in a set of agreements. The system highlights candidate clauses and links each one to its contract, allowing the reviewer to inspect the wording and decide which agreements need attention.

usedIn.name: Contract review
usedIn.detail: Finding and extracting relevant clauses for reviewers to assess.

usedIn.name: E-discovery
usedIn.detail: Searching and organizing documents that may be relevant to a legal matter.

usedIn.name: Legal research
usedIn.detail: Helping locate passages and materials related to a research question.

usedIn.name: Compliance monitoring
usedIn.detail: Reviewing records and flagging items that may need attention.

explainer.intuition: Legal work often involves finding a small amount of important information in many documents. AI can help narrow that search and organize what it finds, but its suggestions still need checking against the original material and the legal context.
howItWorks: Provide contracts, case-related documents, research questions, or compliance records.
The system searches, classifies, extracts, or summarizes information for the chosen task.
It returns relevant passages, candidate clauses, organized document sets, or alerts.
A reviewer checks the outputs against the source material before using them in legal work.
explainer.whyItMatters: It can make document-heavy legal tasks easier to search, organize, and prioritize. Human review remains important because a missed passage or mistaken interpretation can change the result of the work.
misconceptions: It is not limited to legal research; the term also covers contract review, e-discovery, and compliance monitoring.
An AI-generated answer or alert is not automatically a reliable legal conclusion.
Finding a relevant passage is not the same as understanding how it applies to a particular legal situation.
